grass_field.h.what: The first grass_crush_sim() call throws away every tick recorded before it, and under --shot that call is the only one there will ever be, so every screenshot the project takes of this feature has a completely empty crush field.
grass_field.h.where: grass_field.h:1112, `nticks = 0;` inside the `if (fresh)` block, with its premise stated at grass_field.h:1112 ("a queue recorded against the old field") and grass_field.h:1053-1055
grass_field.h.why: game_run_shot (cnc_eyes.cpp:28490) runs every warm-up tick at cnc_eyes.cpp:28504-28524 with NO drawn frame, and then calls draw_frame exactly once at cnc_eyes.cpp:28594 before grab_and_write. grass_crush_sim() lives in draw_frame, so its first call is always the `fresh` one. Nothing draws before it: the dispatch at cnc_eyes.cpp:32766 goes game_boot then straight into game_run_shot, and none of the other draw_frame call sites (24798, 24947, 26232, 26742, 28875, 32157) is on that path. My probe reproduced the exact order and measured cover G=0.000, cover max over the whole map 0.000 and tread max R=0.000 at 20, 120 and 300 warm-up ticks alike. The premise is also false: CrushVeh and CrushRect are in CELLS (grass_field.h:330-337), so they do not depend on the field's resolution and nothing about them is stale.
grass_field.h.consequence: grass_crush_sim() returns 1, so the grass draws, but with a cover channel that is zero everywhere. That is precisely the state the file's own header (grass_field.h:76-84) says is broken grass: every blade overlapping a building or a unit inverts the keystone, so every --shot and the first shot of every gate script shows a dark halo one blade tall around every building and every vehicle, plus grass standing through them, plus no tread marks at all. G36c passes vacuously, because a uniformly empty field digests identically five times. The live loop gets the same failure for one frame at mission start, and because grass_field.h:1109 also clears g_crushPrev, for a second tick after that no vehicle has a previous position so no tread is laid either (my probe: cover recovers to 1.000 on the second drawn frame, tread is still 0.000).
grass_field.h.fix: Delete the `nticks = 0;` at grass_field.h:1112 and let the queue replay onto the freshly cleared target, which clearFirst has already cleared. Keep g_crushPrev too (drop grass_field.h:1109). The one case the line was defending against, a queue recorded under the PREVIOUS mission, is a mission-change problem and belongs in a mission-change reset: call grass_crush_reset() from game_shutdown and game_load_slot, beside dmg_reset() and shatter_reset(), which is the placement cnc_eyes.cpp:9608-9613 already prescribes for exactly this class of surviving state.

grass_field.h.what: g_crushHullCache is keyed on a pack mesh index and is deliberately never dropped, so from the second mission of a process onward every vehicle gets whatever hull the previous pack had at that index.
grass_field.h.where: grass_field.h:382 (`static std::map<int, CrushHull> g_crushHullCache;`), the cache write at grass_field.h:411, and the claim that justifies it at grass_field.h:539-540 ("The hull cache is NOT dropped: it is a pure function of the mesh, and the meshes belong to the pack")
grass_field.h.why: The repository has already paid for this exact mistake twice and says so in two places. cnc_eyes.cpp:9600-9613: "THE CACHES ARE MESH INDICES INTO g_pack, SO THEY CANNOT OUTLIVE THE PACK. pack_free invalidates every index and the next mission's load_pack renumbers them", with the measured case of ION0..ION9 at mesh 227..236 becoming DBRS1..DBRV3 in 98 other packs. cnc_eyes.cpp:19297-19303 repeats it for g_dmgCache and records that the fix was believed to be in place for a year while it was not. load_pack resizes tex/mesh/cell (cnc_eyes.cpp:2215, 2230). My probe measured it directly: mesh index 0 built from an MTNK-shaped mesh caches beam 0.514, and after the pack is replaced with a bike-sized mesh at the same index the cache still returns 0.514 where the correct answer is 0.289.
grass_field.h.consequence: The cover rectangle at grass_field.h:911-921 is sized from the cached beam and length. A vehicle whose stale cached hull is too small has its flanks outside the cover, so contract B inverts along both sides of it: the dark halo the whole skirt mechanism exists to prevent, on every affected vehicle, from mission two onward and on every save loaded from a different mission. The track gauge and band width are the wrong vehicle's as well, so a Recon Bike lays Mammoth tracks or the reverse. It is silent, and it never happens in a single-mission --shot, so no gate would catch it.
grass_field.h.fix: Clear g_crushHullCache wherever the pack changes. Simplest correct form: add `g_crushHullCache.clear();` to grass_crush_free at grass_field.h:522-536, and call grass_crush_reset() from game_shutdown and game_load_slot beside dmg_reset() and shatter_reset(), which is where cnc_eyes.cpp:9608-9613 says this kind of cache has to be reset. Then correct the comment at grass_field.h:539-540, because as written it will be believed by the next reader.

grass_field.h.what: The shroud channel is re-emitted over the whole map on every engine tick with no test of whether the shroud actually changed, and it is the single most expensive thing in the pass, not the free one the comment claims.
grass_field.h.where: grass_field.h:994-1010 (crush_shroud_write), its trigger at grass_field.h:1005-1012 (crush_shroud_dirty compares only the tick number and the rectangle, never the content), and the cost claim at grass_field.h:231-235
grass_field.h.why: Measured on an AMD Radeon PRO W6800X. The full-map shroud strip costs 0.150 ms of the 0.190 ms tick at 62x62 (79 per cent) and 0.370 ms of the 0.481 ms tick at 128x128 (77 per cent). I then rebuilt the same file with -DGRASS_CRUSH_MAXBYTES=1048576, which shrinks the 128-cell field from 2048x2048 to 256x256, one sixty-fourth of the texels: the shroud share was 0.366 ms, unchanged. So the cost is not fill, it is immediate-mode submission, 66,048 glVertex2f plus glColor4f calls an engine tick at 128 cells. The comment at grass_field.h:233 counts those very vertices and calls them "nothing". Two further facts: 128x128 costs 2.6x what 256x256 costs, so the constant at grass_field.h:235 makes the larger map the cheap one; and the engine already publishes the content signal this pass needs, g_shroudCornersDirty and g_shroudCornersMode in shroud_corners_sync at shroud_mod.h:520-528, which the file never asks.
grass_field.h.consequence: 0.370 ms of a 1.6 ms frame budget, 23 per cent of a whole frame, spent every engine tick on a 128x128 map to rewrite a channel that on nearly every tick is bit for bit what it already was. At 60 fps and 15 Hz that lands as a 0.48 ms hitch on one frame in four; at game speed 6 it is 13.0 ms of every wall second and a hitch 27 times a second. On the 62x62 shipped maps it is 0.150 ms of every tick for the same nothing.
grass_field.h.fix: Ask the shroud whether it moved before redrawing it. Call shroud_corners_sync() and capture g_shroudCornersMode plus a corner-field generation counter (g_shroudCornersDirty already exists at shroud_mod.h:505-528 and is set by shroud_set_world_grid and by every reveal), store them beside g_crushShroudFrame, and return early from crush_shroud_pass when neither they nor the rectangle changed. On the measurement above that takes the whole pass to 0.040 ms a tick at 62 cells and 0.111 ms at 128 cells. While there, either raise GRASS_CRUSH_SHROUD_FULL_CELLS above 128x128 or lower it below, because 16384 is not greater than 16384 and the size that pays the most is the one the constant nominates as free.

grass_field.h.what: The two life dials are documented and printed in seconds but their step is per TICK, and the tick rate is a player-facing slider that ranges over a factor of 3.6, so a mark's life follows the game speed rather than the clock.
grass_field.h.where: grass_field.h:221 (`#define GRASS_CRUSH_TICKS_HZ 15.0f`), its use in crush_step_for_life at grass_field.h:452, the dial rows and ladder documented in seconds at grass_field.h:252-283, and the debug print at grass_field.h:1278-1279
grass_field.h.why: The tick rate is not fixed at 15. cnc_eyes.cpp:29110-29112 is `static const double SPEED_HZ[DOPT_MAX_SPEED] = { 7.5, 10.0, 12.5, 15.0, 18.0, 22.0, 27.0 };` and cnc_eyes.cpp:32077 schedules the next tick with `next_tick += 1000.0 / SPEED_HZ[game_speed_setting()]`, read fresh every tick so that dragging the slider takes effect immediately (cnc_eyes.cpp:29107-29109). The setting is persisted for players through game_controls_remember (cnc_eyes.cpp:15911-15922). My probe computed the achieved life of the default 60 s tread dial at each setting: 136.5 s at speed 0, 68.3 s at the default speed 3, and 37.9 s at speed 6.
grass_field.h.consequence: A tread the panel says lasts 60 seconds lasts 37.9 at speed 6 and 136.5 at speed 0, and the same spread applies to the regrowth dial, so the feature is tuned at one speed and wrong at the other six. The CRUSHDBG line at grass_field.h:1278-1279 prints the speed-3 number whatever the speed, so anyone tuning off it is reading a figure that does not describe the run. The per-tick cost measured above is also paid 27 times a second instead of 15 at the top setting, 1.8x the load.
grass_field.h.fix: Make crush_step_for_life read the live rate instead of the constant: pass SPEED_HZ[game_speed_setting()] in where GRASS_CRUSH_TICKS_HZ is used at grass_field.h:452, keep the same quantisation onto the 2^-11 grid, and recompute the step in grass_crush_sim each call so a slider drag takes effect on the next tick. Determinism is untouched: the speed setting is an input to the run, not a clock, and cnc_eyes.cpp:15915-15921 already guarantees no automated run picks up a remembered one. Fix the same divisor in the debug print at grass_field.h:1278-1279.

grass_field.h.what: A refused half-float target is retried in full on every drawn frame, for the life of the mission, with an unlatched error message.
grass_field.h.where: grass_field.h:1101-1103 (the crush_rt_init call inside the fresh block) together with grass_field.h:1053-1055 and grass_field.h:508-518
grass_field.h.why: crush_rt_init returns 0 before g_crushW is assigned at grass_field.h:1105, and its failure path calls fx_rt_free, which zeroes rt->w, rt->h, rt->tex and rt->fbo (fx_gl.h, fx_rt_free). So on the next frame `fresh` at grass_field.h:1053 is still true (w != g_crushW, which is still 0), the guard at grass_field.h:1057 does not fire because fresh is true, and the whole allocation runs again: glGenTextures, four glTexParameteri, a glTexImage2D of up to 32 MiB, an FBO create, a completeness check and an fx_rt_free. The fprintf at grass_field.h:513-515 has no `static int said` latch, unlike the texture-ceiling message at grass_field.h:1065-1071 and the halve message at grass_field.h:1114-1116 which both have one.
grass_field.h.consequence: On a driver that will not give an RGBA16F FBO, every frame allocates and frees up to 32 MiB of texture memory and writes a line to stderr: 60 allocation and free cycles and 60 log lines a second, for the whole mission. That is a hard driver stall on every frame on exactly the machine that is already the weakest, and a log that buries whatever else went wrong.
grass_field.h.fix: Latch the failure. Add a file-scope `static int g_crushDead = 0;`, set it in the crush_rt_init failure branch at grass_field.h:1101-1103, and return 0 at the top of grass_crush_sim while it is set (clearing it only in grass_crush_free so a new mission may retry once). Give the message at grass_field.h:513 the same `static int said` latch the other two messages already have.

grass_field.h.what: The B channel carries only HALF of the shroud attenuation the ground receives, so the part of the blade that stands above the blanket is too bright along the whole reveal edge. The ground is darkened twice: draw_terrain multiplies its vertex light by shroud_corner_vis (cnc_eyes.cpp:6800-6815), and shroud_draw_soft then blends black over it at the SAME per-corner coverage, clamped to SHROUD_SOFT_MAXA 0.784 (shroud_mod.h:722-726, 486). This file writes only the first factor.
grass_field.h.where: grass_field.h:994-1006 (crush_shroud_write writes shroud_corner_vis raw), asserted as exact at grass_field.h:17 and 937-941
grass_field.h.why: The blanket rides ground+0.11 with depth writes off (shroud_mod.h:363, 643, 673-676; cnc_eyes.cpp:1513) and is drawn at cnc_eyes.cpp:20980, after the grass slot at 20390-20394. A blade point is nearer than the lid exactly when it is above 0.11, so the blanket applies its factor to the bottom of the blade and not to the top. The blade's own factor from B is vis = 1-a, while the ground ends at vis*(1-a).
grass_field.h.consequence: In the feather band round the entire revealed area, the exposed top of every blade is 1/(1-a) brighter than its own base and than the ground it stands on, up to 4.63x at the 0.784 clamp. The exposed fraction is (h-0.11)/h: 15 per cent at the default grass_height 0.13 (about 0.9 screen px at 66 px/cell), 45 per cent at 0.20, 69 per cent at the dial's ceiling 0.35 (grass_dials.h:61), and 73 per cent of the 0.414-cell blade the locked contract itself names. That is the bright fringe of grass along the reveal edge this file's own header (grass_field.h:23-33) says the shared array prevents.
grass_field.h.fix: The A channel is reserved and unread (grass_field.h:18). Write the blanket's own factor into it, 1 - min(1-vis, SHROUD_SOFT_MAXA) with the SHROUD_SOFT_OPAQ test copied from shroud_mod.h:722-726, and have the blade multiply by that factor blended in over the lid height, i.e. only on the part of the blade above 0.11 cells (the blade knows its own height above its root). The cheap alternative is to cap the drawn blade height below the lid (0.105 cells) so the blanket covers the whole blade and B = vis becomes exactly right; do NOT raise the lid instead, because a lid at 0.414 displaces the reveal edge about 16 px up-screen from the ground it is meant to cover.
grass_field.h.lens: Lighting and visual maths: one blade fragment traced through fx_post.h, contract A's keystone, contract B's skirt, the root, the shroud channel, and the skirt arithmetic against the engine's camera constants.

grass_field.h.what: On the hard shroud path the channel is 1.0 over the whole map while the blanket still paints opaque black, which is the exact failure the channel exists to prevent.
grass_field.h.where: grass_field.h:1001-1002, and the claim of exactness at grass_field.h:937-941
grass_field.h.why: shroud_corner_vis returns 1.0f unconditionally when !g_shroudSoft (shroud_mod.h:577), because the hard path has no per-corner term. shroud_dispatch_draw still draws a blanket in that mode, calling shroud_draw (cnc_eyes.cpp:18100-18102), whose HIDDEN pass is unblended pure black quads at SHROUD_BLACK_Y (shroud_mod.h:428-436). g_shroudSoft is reachable at runtime from --hardshroud (cnc_eyes.cpp:27013) and from the script verb at cnc_eyes.cpp:24923, and gate G17 exists to compare the two paths.
grass_field.h.consequence: With --hardshroud, fully lit blade tips stand on top of the opaque black over every unexplored cell, at maximum contrast, over the whole unexplored map. Same defect the whole B channel was added for, reached by a switch nobody tested. It is also silent: no GL error, nothing in the log.
grass_field.h.fix: In crush_shroud_write, when !g_shroudSoft take the per-cell state instead of the corner average (shroud_state_at / shroud_opacity, shroud_mod.h:490-500), writing 1 - opacity per cell as a flat quad; or refuse to run the grass at all when !g_shroudSoft and say so on stderr, the way the file already refuses without glBlendEquation.
grass_field.h.lens: Lighting and visual maths: one blade fragment traced through fx_post.h, contract A's keystone, contract B's skirt, the root, the shroud channel, and the skirt arithmetic against the engine's camera constants.

grass_field.h.what: The skirt is spent preventing a halo that cannot occur at the draw slot the design chose, and the one place where the keystone really does invert, the void past the last drawn cell, is the one this file never stamps.
grass_field.h.where: grass_field.h:415-447 (the skirt's stated purpose and crush_skirt_cells) and grass_field.h:1214-1232 (only building runs and vehicle hulls are stamped)
grass_field.h.why: The grass draws between draw_smudges and draw_tiberium_solid (cnc_eyes.cpp:20389-20394). Every object mesh is drawn AFTER it, opaque and depth-written (the opaque pass at cnc_eyes.cpp:20424-20485, walls and wrecks below it, the cutout pass after that). A blade writes no depth, so at any pixel where a blade overlaps a silhouette the depth buffer still holds the terrain behind, the object's fragment is nearer, it passes the depth test and overwrites both colour and depth. No blade colour survives at any pixel whose final depth belongs to a building, a vehicle, a wall, an infantryman or a tree, so gn.a at every surviving blade pixel is the terrain's 1.0. The exception is the void: nothing is drawn past cell_shown's rect + margin (cnc_eyes.cpp:6477-6491), so there d >= 0.99999 and fx_post.h:236 returns the colour before shadow, cloud, lambert, occlusion and point lights alike.
grass_field.h.consequence: Cost paid for nothing: a bare margin of blade_height*1.6507 = 0.215 cells, about 14 px at 66 px/cell, cleared round every building AND round every vehicle, with a hard step from full-height grass to nothing (the cover quads have no shoulder, unlike the tread bands). On a moving Medium Tank the hull cover plus skirt is a 0.94-cell bald band against a 0.514-cell hull, so a vehicle's passage reads as a bald swathe 1.8x its own beam for the first 17 seconds and the carefully one-texel-floored tread bands inside it are invisible until the cover has decayed. Failure not covered: blade tips leaning past the outermost drawn cell keep raw albedo beside neighbours that are shaded and occluded, which shows whenever the shroud is off, revealed at mission end, or in the editor (shroud_corner_vis returns 1.0 in all three, shroud_mod.h:571-579).
grass_field.h.fix: Keep the cover stamp at the hull and the footprint and drop the skirt from both (dial default 0) unless a picture shows grass poking out of a silhouette for some other reason; and add the border case, which is the real one, by calling grass_crush_note_rect for a one-blade-height band just inside the boundary of the drawn terrain (cell_shown's rect + margin, or the grid edge when g_clip_to_map is off). The note_rect hook is already there and already drained per tick.
grass_field.h.lens: Lighting and visual maths: one blade fragment traced through fx_post.h, contract A's keystone, contract B's skirt, the root, the shroud channel, and the skirt arithmetic against the engine's camera constants.

grass_field.h.what: GRASS_CRUSH_PITCH_FLAT is documented as the flattest camera the rig reaches, but 0.92 rad is the STEEPEST of the two console pitches, and the constant is not a bound on the pitch this tier can actually reach.
grass_field.h.why: cnc_eyes.cpp:5456-5458 gives pitch = 0.78 .. 0.92 radians (44.691 .. 52.712 deg) lerped from the zoom distance, and n64_pitch is documented at cnc_eyes.cpp:5525 as radians, positive = looking down, so 0.92 is the most top-down and 0.78 the flattest. The required clearance is h*cot(pitch), which grows as the camera flattens: 1.011h at 0.78 against the 1.651h the file provides. But grass is ENHANCED-only, and under ENHANCED the isometric row replaces the lerp with g_fx.iso_pitch, floored only at cam_fovy_deg()*0.5+2 (cnc_eyes.cpp:5531-5536), which is 26 degrees at the shipped iso_fov 48; the dial's own range is 0..85 (fx_state.h:622). The editor's g_camPitchFree is unbounded below as well.
grass_field.h.consequence: cot(26 deg) is 2.05, so at the flat end of the isometric dial the geometry needs 0.267 cells of clearance where the file gives 0.215, and the file's stated 39 to 117 per cent margin becomes a 20 per cent shortfall. Today that costs nothing visible because the objects overwrite those pixels (see the previous finding), but the comment is the reason nobody looked, and the moment the grass moves to a slot after the object passes, which is what grass occluding a unit's feet would require, the halo is live at flat isometric tilts and at any editor pitch below 31.2 degrees.
grass_field.h.fix: Compute the skirt from cot, not sec, and from the flattest pitch this tier can actually reach: max over N64_PITCH_AT_NEAR and, when cam_option_active(), the isometric floor, i.e. s = blade_height / tanf(pitch_min) * skirt. Correct the comment: 0.92 is the steepest console pitch, 0.78 the flattest.
grass_field.h.lens: Lighting and visual maths: one blade fragment traced through fx_post.h, contract A's keystone, contract B's skirt, the root, the shroud channel, and the skirt arithmetic against the engine's camera constants.

grass_field.h.what: On the first drawn frame after a scenario load the pass clears the field, throws the entire recorded tick queue away, stamps nothing, and still returns 1, so the grass is told to draw against a cover channel that is 0.0 everywhere.
grass_field.h.where: grass_field.h:1108 and 1112 (the queue clear and nticks = 0 inside the fresh block at 1100-1130), reached with the success return at 1282
grass_field.h.why: Measured on a real GL 2.1 context with my own probe, a scratch probe, which stages a building footprint in g_bldCellNow and a parked MTNK, records twelve ticks, then calls grass_crush_sim once: it returns 1 while the field reads G = 0.0000 under the building centre and G = 0.0000 under the tank, and G = 1.0000 on the very next frame. The author's own gl_probe never sees this because its fresh_field() helper at gl_probe.cpp burns the fresh frame before every test. The overflow path at grass_field.h:1066-1075 does the opposite and correctly clears the field and still replays its one queued tick, so the fresh path is the only one that leaves the cover channel empty.
grass_field.h.consequence: Every blade inside every building footprint and every vehicle hull stands unclipped on that frame, which is exactly the condition contract B exists to prevent: the scene depth belongs to the object, the ground normal alpha is 0, the ground lambert is skipped and the occlusion weight doubles, so every building and unit wears the dark halo one blade tall. In interactive play that is one to four drawn frames at every mission start and every scenario change. Under a scripted shot it is every shot: cnc_eyes.cpp:26232 and 28875 draw exactly one frame and grab it, so a gate screenshot's only frame is always the fresh frame and every visual gate for grass would capture the broken picture instead of the shipped one.
grass_field.h.fix: Do not discard the queue on a fresh field. The recorded rects and vehicles are in cell coordinates and the clear has already run, so replaying them onto the freshly cleared field is safe and is what the overflow path already does: delete the g_crushVeh/g_crushRect/g_crushTick clear at 1108 and the nticks = 0 at 1112. If the queue really must be dropped, for instance because a scenario change can carry the previous mission's rects, then return 0 for that one frame so the grass does not draw, which is the rule the file's own header states.
grass_field.h.lens: GL correctness and state (entry points, enum legality, GLSL 1.20 legality, state save/restore, CLASSIC and Win98 compile and byte-identical draw)

grass_field.h.what: When the half-float target is refused, nothing records that the attempt was made, so the whole allocation path and its stderr line run again on every drawn frame instead of once. The failure message is also the only one in the file with no once-guard.
grass_field.h.where: grass_field.h:512-516 (the unguarded fprintf) together with 1101-1104 (the failure return leaves g_crushW and g_crushH at 0, and they are only assigned at 1105 on success, so `fresh` at 1053-1057 recomputes true forever)
grass_field.h.why: Measured by forcing the refusal in a private copy of the header (PROBE_ONLY_forced_failure_copy.h, one line changed, plus verify_retry.cpp, both in the same directory): 300 simulated drawn frames produced 300 identical "GRASS|crush|half-float target 992x992 refused" lines on stderr and re-entered glGenTextures, glTexImage2D, glGenFramebuffers, glDeleteTextures and glDeleteFramebuffers 300 times. Every other failure message in this same file is once-guarded (grass_field.h:154 via g_crushGlTried, 1043 and 1069 via static ints, 1113 via g_crushHalveSaid, 807 and 826 via static ints), so this is an inconsistency inside the file rather than a judgement call.
grass_field.h.consequence: On a driver that refuses RGBA16F as a colour attachment, which is the exact case the message is written for, "the grass stays off" becomes an unbounded stderr flood at frame rate, about 3600 lines a minute at 60 fps, which buries every other diagnostic a --script run prints and which the gate scripts read. It also re-runs a texture and framebuffer allocate-and-free every drawn frame for the life of the session: harmless in time on this driver (0.016 ms a frame measured, because the storage is never touched), but a 7.5 MiB allocation on a 62-cell map and 32 MiB on a 128-cell map on any driver that commits the storage eagerly.
grass_field.h.fix: Add a tried-and-failed flag next to g_crushGlTried that grass_crush_sim tests before it reaches the allocation, cleared only by grass_crush_reset, and put a `static int said` guard on the fprintf at 513 in the same shape as the five other messages in the file.
grass_field.h.lens: GL correctness and state (entry points, enum legality, GLSL 1.20 legality, state save/restore, CLASSIC and Win98 compile and byte-identical draw)

grass_field.h.what: Six of the nine states crush_gl_save reads are not given a default before their query, while three of them are given one for exactly this reason.
grass_field.h.where: grass_field.h:755-762 (colMask, srcRGB, dstRGB, srcA, dstA, eqRGB, eqA) against 753, 769 and 773, which do pre-initialise depthMask, bind2d and prog
grass_field.h.why: GL_BLEND_SRC_RGB, GL_BLEND_DST_RGB, GL_BLEND_SRC_ALPHA and GL_BLEND_DST_ALPHA are GL 1.4 state and GL_BLEND_EQUATION_ALPHA is GL 2.0 state, but the file's own gate for reaching this code is that glBlendEquationEXT resolved, and EXT_blend_minmax does not imply GL 1.4. fx_gl.h:212-226 accepts the ARB shader-object spellings, so fx_gl_ready can be satisfied below GL 2.0 as well. On such a context glGetIntegerv raises GL_INVALID_ENUM and leaves the field holding whatever was on the stack. I could not produce a driver like that here, so this is a mechanism I can point at rather than one I reproduced; on the GL 2.1 target every enum is valid and I confirmed the restore is exact.
grass_field.h.consequence: crush_gl_restore at 822 then calls glBlendFunc with an uninitialised GLint. A rejected glBlendFunc is a no-op, so the blend function stays at the pass's own GL_ONE, GL_ONE and every translucent draw after the grass in that frame, the shroud blanket, the tiberium decals and the tree cutouts, composites additively. That reads as a lighting bug somewhere else entirely, which is the same failure shape the blend-equation restore comment at 796-800 is written to avoid.
grass_field.h.fix: Give all six the GL defaults before the query, the same one line the file already spends on the other three: colMask all GL_TRUE, srcRGB and srcA GL_ONE, dstRGB and dstA GL_ZERO, eqRGB and eqA GL_FUNC_ADD.
grass_field.h.lens: GL correctness and state (entry points, enum legality, GLSL 1.20 legality, state save/restore, CLASSIC and Win98 compile and byte-identical draw)

grass_draw.h.what: The crush field is paid for in full on every map and every setting where grass can never draw. The call-site contract this file writes puts grass_crush_sim() unconditionally on the line above grass_draw(), and every gate that could decline the feature lives inside grass_draw, after the field has already been allocated and stepped.
grass_draw.h.where: grass_draw.h:90-93 (the two-line call-site contract) with grass_draw.h:607-611 (the gates that run after it)
grass_draw.h.why: grass_crush_sim gates only on g_fxActive, fx_gl_ready and the grid (grass_field.h:1024-1027); it never reads g_fx.grass or g_grassHave. grass_field.h:566 writes the master-toggle gate out as example text inside a comment and never implements it. Meanwhile grass_bake returns false and leaves g_grassHave 0 for any grid over 128 cells (grass_bake.h:1075-1091) and any buffer over 48 MiB (grass_bake.h:845-858), which is the 256x256 pack and both 128x128 packs. The costs are the file's own probe numbers, probe_out.txt section 11 and the table at grass_field.h:188-193.
grass_draw.h.consequence: On the 256x256 pack, where the bake has refused and not one blade will ever draw: 32.00 MiB of VRAM held for the run and 0.166 ms of GPU per engine tick, forever, on a field nothing samples. On the two 128x128 packs, also refused: 32.00 MiB and 0.551 ms per tick, which is 34 percent of the 1.6 ms budget spent on the frame that carries the tick, on a map with no grass in it. And on an ordinary 62x62 mission, unticking "real grass" in the F5 panel leaves 7.51 MiB and 0.134 ms a tick in place, so the master toggle turns off the picture and not the cost, and an A/B against it measures the shader rather than the feature.
grass_draw.h.fix: Make the two calls one gated block, and say so in the contract at grass_draw.h:90-93: if (g_fxActive && g_fx.grass && g_grassHave) { grass_crush_sim(); grass_draw(); }. Add the same g_fx.grass test to grass_crush_note_tick, which grass_field.h:563-567 already knows it wants and did not write, so the tick half stops walking the grid fifteen times a second too. A switched-off field is also a cleared one, so the field is correct from the tick after it is switched back on.

grass_draw.h.what: The distance LOD is quantised to the 4-cell tile while the fade band is only 1.6 tiles wide, so the outer edge of the grass is a hard, axis-aligned tile boundary rather than a fade. The comment calling it "smoothstep, never a switch" describes the temporal behaviour, which is fine, not the spatial one, which is not.
grass_draw.h.where: grass_draw.h:548-552 (near_ = far_ * 0.75f, k taken from the tile centre) with grass_draw.h:565-570 (the argument for tile granularity)
grass_draw.h.why: far_ - near_ is 0.25 * grass_fade = 6.5 cells at the default of 26, and GRASS_TILE is 4 (grass_bake.h:127), so the entire fade is sampled 1.6 times. Radial tile centres 4 cells apart give a raw k step of 0.615. Evaluated on the real camera at the far zoom (eye 13.05 cells up, footprint 9.94 cells behind the focus, from n64_pitch and n64_dist_cells at cnc_eyes.cpp:5524-5552 and the constants at :5415-5459), consecutive tile rows carry 96, then 22 to 64, then 0 blades a cell depending on lattice alignment.
grass_draw.h.consequence: The grass horizon is a stair-stepped arc, not a fade: a roughly 59 px band across the upper screen at half density, ending in a straight 4-cell edge with 22 to 64 blades a cell on one side and bare ground on the other. At the dial's minimum grass_fade of 6 the band is 1.5 cells, under half a tile, and the whole field switches off in a single tile row.
grass_draw.h.fix: Keep the count per tile and move the FADE per blade. Add a uCamXZ uniform and fold clamp((uFar - length(root.xz - uCamXZ)) / (uFar - uNear)) into keep at grass_draw.h:317; take the tile's count from its NEAREST corner rather than its centre so the count stays conservative. The file's own objection to a per-vertex distance at grass_draw.h:567-570, that a blade would fade differently at its root than at its tip, does not apply: grass_draw.h:279-281 states that the root is identical on all four corners, so a distance taken from root is constant across the card exactly as keep already is. If that is too much for this slice, floor the band at three tiles: near_ = far_ - (0.25f * far_ > 3.0f * (float)GRASS_TILE ? 0.25f * far_ : 3.0f * (float)GRASS_TILE).

grass_draw.h.what: uEdge is re-uploaded once per tile for a value that cannot change inside the pass. It is g_fx.grass_edge and nothing else, read from the same struct field on every iteration.
grass_draw.h.why: The comment at grass_draw.h:788-790 justifies the position as the call site a future distance-widened ramp will want. Nothing in the loop writes g_fx.grass_edge, so every call after the first uploads the number the program already holds. At the measured 62 drawing tiles (my own frustum and cull-box count on the real camera) that is 61 redundant driver calls a frame.
grass_draw.h.consequence: About 61 wasted fx_glUniform1f calls a frame, roughly 0.02 ms, which is a bit over 1 percent of a 1.6 ms budget spent on nothing. Small, but it is the only line in the pass that pays for a feature that does not exist yet, and the pass is already at about 437 GL calls a frame.
grass_draw.h.fix: Hoist it above the tile loop next to the other fx_set1f calls and set it once. Put it back inside the loop on the day the distance-widened ramp is actually written, at which point it will be carrying a per-tile value and will earn its place.

grass_draw.h.what: uSkirt uses the wrong trigonometric function. The projection needs cot(pitch); the file divides by cos(pitch), which is not merely too generous, it moves the wrong way with the camera and inverts sign of error at low pitch.
grass_draw.h.where: grass_draw.h:694-696 (float cp = cosf(n64_pitch()); if (cp < 0.20f) cp = 0.20f; uSkirt = grass_height / cp), claimed at grass_draw.h:66-70 and 311-317
grass_draw.h.why: The modelview is T(0,0,-D) * Rx(pitch) (game/cnc_eyes.cpp:5862-5864), and n64_pitch is elevation from horizontal, positive looking down (cnc_eyes.cpp:5523). Under Rx(p) a world vertical h contributes h*cos(p) to eye y and a ground step d away from the camera contributes d*sin(p), so a blade tip reaches the screen row of a ground point h*cot(p) away, not h/cos(p). grass_field.h:432-435 derives exactly that and says so, then deliberately freezes 1/cos at a CONSTANT pitch (GRASS_CRUSH_PITCH_FLAT 0.92, grass_field.h:440-447) so the cover skirt cannot breathe; grass_draw.h applies the same wrong factor to the LIVE pitch, so the header's claim at line 68 that the two carry 'the same one-blade skirt' is also false. The two forms cross at 38.17 deg. n64_pitch's reachable range is not the console lerp alone: with the Perspective row on Isometric, iso_pitch is a 0..85 deg dial (fx_state.h:622) floored at cam_fovy_deg()*0.5+2 (cnc_eyes.cpp:5532-5537), i.e. 26 deg at the shipped iso_fov 48 and 14.5 deg at the dial's minimum fov. Measured with grass_height 0.13: at 26 deg the skirt is 0.1446 cells against 0.2665 needed, 54 per cent of it; at 14.5 deg it is 0.134 against 0.503, 27 per cent. In the other direction, at 53 deg it is 2.21x too wide, at 70 deg 8.0x, and past 78.46 deg the cos clamp pins it at 5*height = 0.65 cells against 0.027 needed, 24x. The clamp guards the wrong end: cos is LARGE at small pitch, so `if (cp < 0.20f)` never fires in the regime where the value collapses, and only fires where it should already be near zero.
grass_draw.h.consequence: Below 38 deg of pitch the cleared band is shorter than one blade, so blades overlap the sea, cliff faces, roads and the map rim, the ground-normal alpha there is 0, the one-sun lambert is skipped and the SSAO weight goes 0.5 -> 1.0: the dark halo of contract B comes back along every shoreline and cliff, which is the exact failure the skirt exists to prevent. Above about 60 deg the opposite: at the shipped default pitch (console rig, 44.7 to 52.7 deg) the bald verge is 10.1 to 15.1 screen px where 4.7 to 10.8 is needed, and it WIDENS as the player zooms out while the geometric requirement shrinks, so the bare margin around every shore and cliff breathes the wrong way with the zoom. Worse, uSkirt can exceed the bake's own saturation: sd saturates at 0.718 cells (grass_bake.h:374-386, stated at grass_bake.h:1206), so for any grass_height above 0.15 cells at a pitch above about 78 deg (0.20 cells above 74 deg, 0.35 cells above 61 deg) smoothstep(0, uSkirt, sd) never reaches 1.0 for ANY blade on the map and the entire field, including the middle of open ground far from any edge, drops to a uniform partial alpha: at grass_height 0.35 and 80 deg every blade in the game is drawn at 0.366 alpha.
grass_draw.h.fix: Use the cotangent: float tp = tanf(n64_pitch()); if (tp < 0.35f) tp = 0.35f; uSkirt = grass_height * generosity / tp. Floor the TANGENT, not the cosine, so the guard bites at shallow pitch where the value explodes. Then clamp the result to the bake's own saturation, uSkirt = min(uSkirt, grass_sd_range_of(cfg)), so the fade band can never exceed the range sd can express, and say so once on stderr the way grass_build's index abort already does when it clamps. Keep a deliberate generosity factor (grass_field.h's argument for one is sound) but as an explicit multiplier, not smuggled in as the wrong trig function.
grass_draw.h.lens: Lighting and visual maths: one blade fragment traced through fx_post.h, the keystone of contract A, the silhouette halo of contract B, the root-to-ground match, the shroud channel against the blanket, and the screen-scale arithmetic against the engine's camera constants.

grass_draw.h.what: The root fade does not make the root match the ground. The AO, tip and gain multiplies are applied AFTER the root blend, so at b2t = 0 the blade is 0.45x the ground colour, not the ground colour.
grass_draw.h.where: grass_draw.h:424 then 431-433 (vec3 col = mix(vGnd.rgb, body, smoothstep(0.0, uRootFade, b2t)); col *= (1.0 - uAO) + uAO * b2t; col *= 1.0 + uTip * b2t * b2t; gl_FragColor = vec4(col * uGain, a);), claimed at grass_draw.h:415-420
grass_draw.h.why: The header states 'At b2t = 0 the blade IS the ground under it, so there is nothing to sort and nothing to see through'. Substituting the shipped defaults from the blade agent's grass_dials.h (grass_ao 0.55, grass_root_fade 0.22, grass_tint 0.85, grass_gain 1.0), col at b2t = 0 is vGnd.rgb * ((1 - 0.55) + 0) * 1.0 = 0.45 * the ground colour. The ramp that is supposed to hide the junction is the mix on line 424, but line 431 multiplies straight through it. At the lowest sampled fragment of a far-zoom blade (b2t = 0.5/3.71 = 0.135, from the 3.71 px height the header itself derives) the value is 0.47 * ground + 0.053 * own, painted at alpha ~1.0 because the root ALPHA ramp is dead (see the separate finding), so the bottom scanline of every blade is a hard step from 1.0 * ground to about 0.5 * ground across one pixel boundary. uGain compounds it in the other direction: at its dial maximum of 2.00 the root is 2x the ground it grows out of. Because grass_tint is 0.85 the blade body is 85 per cent the ground colour anyway, so this AO term is essentially the field's whole visual signal, and it is landing on the one band the design says must be invisible.
grass_draw.h.consequence: A dark line at the foot of every blade, exactly the artefact the root fade is written to remove, multiplied by 96 blades a cell into a dense dark stipple that makes the grass read as a dirty layer over the ground rather than as growing out of it. Worse for shimmer than for tone: the blade's bottom edge falls at a random sub-pixel phase per blade, so which pixel row takes the 0.45 step moves per blade and crawls as the camera pans, which is the temporal fault the header's own design argument at lines 25-33 claims to have avoided.
grass_draw.h.fix: Ramp the shading with the same curve as the colour, so both reach the ground at b2t = 0: float rf = smoothstep(0.0, uRootFade, b2t); vec3 col = mix(vGnd.rgb, body, rf); col *= mix(1.0, ((1.0 - uAO) + uAO * b2t) * (1.0 + uTip * b2t * b2t) * uGain, rf); Equivalently, apply AO, tip and gain to `body` before the mix on line 424. Either form leaves every dial live and makes the root genuinely equal to vGnd.rgb.

grass_draw.h.what: Both softening ramps are narrower than one pixel at their own defaults, so neither does the job the file assigns it and the blade is in practice a hard-edged sub-pixel column.
grass_draw.h.where: grass_draw.h:410-411 (a = 1.0 - smoothstep(1.0 - uEdge, 1.0, abs(vShape.y)); a *= smoothstep(0.0, uRootAlpha, b2t);), argued at grass_draw.h:25-33 and 403-409
grass_draw.h.why: Using the header's own screen scale, verified against cnc_eyes.cpp:5415-5462 and 5854-5864: a blade is 3.71 to 7.61 px tall and its card half width at the root is 1.06 to 1.85 px face-on, 0.67 to 1.18 px averaged over the baked yaw. uEdge's default is 0.30 (grass_dials.h:121), and the ramp runs over 0.30 of the HALF width, so it is 0.20 to 0.35 px at the root and 0.06 to 0.11 px at the tip after the 0.30 taper. uRootAlpha's proposed default is 0.06 of the blade height, so 0.22 to 0.46 px; the lowest fragment centre of a far-zoom blade sits at b2t = 0.5/3.71 = 0.135, and smoothstep(0, 0.06, 0.135) is exactly 1.0, so that ramp never touches a sampled fragment at all. The engine offers no help: the GL attributes ask for double buffer, 24-bit depth and 8/8/8 and no multisample, which the header states and I did not find contradicted.
grass_draw.h.consequence: The alpha ramp the design chose instead of an alpha test is below the sampling grid at both ends, so the card is a 1 to 2 px hard-edged column and the far field crawls as the camera pans, which is precisely the failure the design claims to have engineered around. The root alpha ramp is a control that does nothing at its default, and where a blade's bottom edge happens to fall just under a pixel centre it fires on one blade and not its neighbour, adding a per-blade random dimming rather than the smooth join it promises.
grass_draw.h.fix: Make uEdge a SCREEN-space ramp, which is the call site the file already prepared: the per-tile block at grass_draw.h:786-790 knows the tile's distance, so compute pxPerCell = 0.5f * fbh * cam_f() / dist, halfWidthPx = 0.5f * g_fx.grass_width * pxPerCell * 0.6366f, and set uEdge = clamp(rampPx / max(halfWidthPx, 1e-3), g_fx.grass_edge, 1.0f) with rampPx about 1.0. That is one line at an existing call site and needs no shader change. Re-range grass_root_alpha so its default is at least one pixel of blade, about 0.15 rather than 0.06, or drive it from the same per-tile pixel height.

grass_draw.h.what: Trees are in neither of the two halo-prevention mechanisms the file names, so the keystone inverts along the underside of every canopy and around every trunk.
grass_draw.h.where: grass_draw.h:60-72 ('THE FIX IS GEOMETRIC AND IT IS IN TWO PLACES ... STATIC EDGES water, cliffs, roads and the map rim ... MOVING EDGES buildings and vehicles') and grass_draw.h:73-74 ('If a halo appears at a wall's foot, the bug is in the skirt or the cover channel')
grass_draw.h.why: The static list is the bake's blocked-cell mask, which is the CLEAR1 texel mask plus the water veto plus the map border (grass_bake.h:617-622, 681-700); it has no object term. The cover channel is g_bldCellNow, which is K_BUILDING only (grass_field.h:661 and the note at :655-662), plus CrushVeh, which grass_field.h:640 and :663 restrict to K_UNIT, plus grass_crush_note_rect, whose own comment at grass_field.h:550-556 says 'none of them is in this file's scope, so the hook is here and the caller is elsewhere', i.e. unwired. Trees are K_TERRAIN and are drawn by tree3d_draw in the CUTOUT pass at cnc_eyes.cpp:20605-20608, which is BEFORE the grass call site at 20639 and writes depth, so a blade standing on the camera side of a trunk or under the lower rim of a canopy blends over it and passes its depth test. tree3d_draw_normals then stamps that pixel with uNormAlpha = 0.5 (cnc_eyes.cpp:8046-8059), which in the light pass gives haveN = 1 and ground = 0 (fx_post.h:232-233): the one-sun lambert at fx_post.h:333-337 is skipped and the occlusion weight becomes ssao_foliage 0.35 instead of ssao_ground 0.5 (fx_post.h:375, defaults at fx_state.h:1046 and :1115). I checked the two neighbouring cases and they are fine: infantry draw at pass 6 (cnc_eyes.cpp:20800), after the grass, so they overdraw it rather than being overlapped by it; walls are K_BUILDING and so are covered by g_bldCellNow.
grass_draw.h.consequence: A fringe one blade tall, 3.5 to 7.6 screen px, along the lower rim of every canopy and around every trunk base, where the grass is lit as foliage instead of as ground. On level ground the lambert is near 1.0 and the visible difference is only the occlusion weight, a few per cent. On a slope it is large: col *= clamp(lam, sun_floor, 1.35) with sun_floor 0.55 (fx_state.h:1040) means the grass beside the tree on a shaded hillside is multiplied by 0.55 and the fringe over the tree by 1.0, an 82 per cent brightness step, so every tree on a shaded slope gets a bright rim of grass around its foot, and on a sunlit slope a darker one. Trees are the most common object on a temperate map and are exactly where grass grows.
grass_draw.h.fix: Either stamp trees into the cover channel, which is one loop over g_objects calling grass_crush_note_rect for each tree3d_claims(o) with a radius from the model and the same skirt the buildings get (that hook exists and is unwired), or bake trees into the static block mask, which is cheaper since a tree does not move. Whichever is chosen, correct the claim at grass_draw.h:60-74 so the next reader does not chase a tree halo in the fragment stage, and add the case to grass_field.h's own test list at :1305.

grass_draw.h.what: The LOD's count and its fade do not name the same number. The vertex stage assumes gl_Color.a IS slot/127 ("already slot / 127", line 269) and computes keep = clamp((uSlotCut - slot) * 127.0, 0, 1), with the host handing it uSlotCut = sc/127. But the bake stores the slot byte as (s*255 + 63)/127, whose normalised value sb/255 is NOT s/127: sb = 2s for s <= 63 and 2s+1 for s >= 64, so the two disagree by up to 0.00195 in [0,1], which the shader's own multiply by 127.0 magnifies to a quarter of a whole slot.
grass_draw.h.where: a scratch probe:317 (the keep expression) with :565 (*slotCut = sc / (GRASS_SLOTS - 1)) and :269 (the comment asserting the byte is slot/127)
grass_draw.h.why: Measured on the reference GL 2.1 context by driving the real GRASS_VS with the real byte encoding and reading vShape.z back. At the instant the host's count first admits slot s (sc = s exactly, so the design requires keep = frac(sc) = 0.0000), the shader returns: s=1 -> 0.0039, s=31 -> 0.1216, s=32 -> 0.1255, s=62 -> 0.2431, s=63 -> 0.2471. From s=64 up the sign flips and the blade is discarded outright (keep <= 0) until sc has travelled a further 0.247 of a slot. The encoding is grass_bake.h:785, `const GLubyte sb = (GLubyte)((s * 255 + 63) / (GRASS_SLOTS - 1));`, and sb(63)=126 against 63/127, sb(64)=129 against 64/127.
grass_draw.h.consequence: Locked contract point D is only three-quarters honoured in the middle of the slot axis. Two measurable effects. (1) In the distance fade band, at every LOD boundary below slot 64 that slot's blades (one per cell, 16 per 4x4 tile) appear at up to 24.7% alpha instead of fading in from zero, which is exactly the pop the cumulative table exists to remove. (2) At any density, the slot immediately below the cut sits permanently at ~0.874 alpha instead of 1.0 (measured: at the default density 96, slot 95 reads 0.874), and the slot at the cut is counted by cum[] and then thrown away by the vertex shader's early-out, so its geometry is fetched and transformed for nothing. Both the draw's own comment at line 317 ("the count and the fade name the same number") and the bake's at 785 ("far inside the fade band") assert this cannot happen; one part in 510 of the range is a quarter of one slot, not a fraction of it.
grass_draw.h.fix: Put both sides on the same axis. Cleanest: have the bake store sb = (GLubyte)(s * 2), which is exact for every s in 0..127, have grass_draw send uSlotCut = sc * (2.0f / 255.0f), and change the shader's scale from * 127.0 to * 127.5. Then slot = 2s/255, uSlotCut = 2sc/255 and (uSlotCut - slot) * 127.5 is exactly sc - s for every slot, with no rounding anywhere. If the bake's encoding must stay, the draw cannot fix this alone and the disagreement should be stated as a known quarter-slot offset in both files rather than asserted away.

grass_draw.h.what: The texture bindings on units 0 and 1 are zeroed on exit rather than restored to what the caller had bound, while the header presents the unbind as part of a one-for-one restore.
grass_draw.h.where: a scratch probe:831-832 (the two glBindTexture(GL_TEXTURE_2D, 0) calls), documented at :105 ("WHAT grass_draw CHANGES AND RESTORES, ONE FOR ONE") and :115 ("texture units 1 and 0 unbound")
grass_draw.h.why: I replayed the pass's exact save/modify/restore block against a baseline reproducing the state at cnc_eyes.cpp:20639 and diffed 30 states. GL_TEXTURE_BINDING_2D was the only one that differed (1 -> 0). In the real frame unit 1 is also affected on the packs that ship a CM layer: draw_terrain's tinted branch binds at.gl to unit 1 at cnc_eyes.cpp:6728-6729 and only disables GL_TEXTURE_2D there on the way out (6853-6856), so the binding survives until grass clears it.
grass_draw.h.consequence: Nothing goes wrong today: every draw after the call site binds its own texture (draw_mesh at cnc_eyes.cpp:8901-8907 does glEnable(GL_TEXTURE_2D) then glBindTexture, the sprite paths at 10259 and 10425 the same), and an enabled unit whose bound object is the incomplete default texture behaves as if texturing were off. The cost is that the header's state contract is not literally true, so the next person auditing this pass against that list will find one item that is a change and not a restore, and any future pass that does rely on an inherited binding will fail here for a reason the contract says is impossible.
grass_draw.h.fix: Either query the two bindings up front (glActiveTexture per unit + glGetIntegerv(GL_TEXTURE_BINDING_2D)) and put them back, which makes the one-for-one claim exact for one extra query a unit, or move these two lines out of the CHANGES-AND-RESTORES list at :105-116 into their own line saying plainly that the pass leaves both units unbound and why that is safe here.
grass_draw.h.lens: GL correctness and state: entry-point legality on GL 2.1 + the two resolved extension groups, enum legality per entry point, GLSL 1.20 conformance, exact state save/restore, and CLASSIC / Win98 compile and byte-identity.

grass_draw.h.what: The paragraph justifying the shroud channel describes a failure mode that cannot occur under the file's own keystone. It says a blade "stands above the lid and depth-rejects the black quad", but the blade is drawn with glDepthMask(GL_FALSE) and writes no depth at all, so it can never reject anything.
grass_draw.h.why: The blanket is drawn by shroud_dispatch_draw at cnc_eyes.cpp:20980, after the grass at 20639, with its own depth writes off (shroud_mod.h:400, 662). Because the grass never won a depth write, the pixel's depth still belongs to the terrain triangle; the blanket rides SHROUD_BLACK_Y = 0.050 above it (shroud_mod.h:363) and is therefore NEARER than the depth it is tested against, so it passes GL_LEQUAL and always draws over the grass. The stated mechanism is the one thing the keystone rules out.
grass_draw.h.consequence: The multiply is still needed, but for a different reason: SHROUD_DARK_ALPHA is 0.45 (shroud_mod.h:357), so a mapped-but-unseen cell lets 55% of whatever is underneath through, which is the same measurement cnc_eyes.cpp:6786-6795 records for the terrain. Anyone who tests the stated claim will not reproduce it (the blanket covers the grass exactly as it covers the ground), and the natural conclusion from that experiment is that the B channel is redundant. Delete it on that basis and every mapped-but-unseen cell grows grass at 55% of full brightness over correctly dimmed ground.
grass_draw.h.fix: Replace the depth-rejection argument with the real one: the blanket is translucent by design, so a blade that was not pre-darkened by the same per-corner coverage byte the terrain takes at cnc_eyes.cpp:6786-6795 would show through it at 55% (78% in the feather band), and the field's B channel is what keeps the blade and the ground under it agreeing before the blanket ever lands.
grass_draw.h.lens: GL correctness and state: entry-point legality on GL 2.1 + the two resolved extension groups, enum legality per entry point, GLSL 1.20 conformance, exact state save/restore, and CLASSIC / Win98 compile and byte-identity.

grass_draw.h.what: Two of the header's load-bearing engine citations point at the wrong lines. The state contract cites cnc_eyes.cpp:20223-20224 for "GL_DEPTH_TEST enabled, GL_LEQUAL", and the keystone cites cnc_eyes.cpp:19760 for fx_draw_terrain_normals.
grass_draw.h.why: cnc_eyes.cpp:20223-20224 is inside fx_gather_lights (L.radius / L.r assignments). The depth state is actually set at cnc_eyes.cpp:20319-20321. fx_draw_terrain_normals is defined at cnc_eyes.cpp:19852, not 19760. The same drift affects the tree3d references at :?, notably cnc_eyes.cpp:7933-7943 for tree3d_arrays_on's host pointers (actually 8017-8020), 7993 for its host index pointer (actually 8189) and 7921 for tree3d_place's wind vector (actually 7944/7951). By contrast every citation below line 6700 and the two at 20639 and 21053 are exact, as are fx_gl.h:419, fx_gl.h:180-186, fx_post.h:233, fx_post.h:333-337, fx_post.h:375, fx_post.h:919-923, shroud_mod.h:363, c3d_ceiling.h:45 and water_mod.h:1530.
grass_draw.h.consequence: The two wrong ones are precisely the citations a reviewer uses to check the file's two central claims: that the depth test is on at the call site, and that the ground-normal pass is the thing the keystone depends on. Following either lands on unrelated code, which reads as the claim being unverifiable rather than as a stale number, and the state contract is the part of this file that most needs to be checkable.

grass_bake.h.what: The skirt width is derived from cos(pitch) at the STEEPEST pitch. The geometry gives cot(pitch), and the worst case is the SHALLOWEST ray in the frame, which is the camera pitch minus the 25 degree half field of view, not the steepest pitch.
grass_bake.h.where: grass_bake.h:368-384 (grass_sd_range_of and its comment), grass_bake.h:287 and :309 (GrassBakeCfg::pitch_max, defaulted to 0.92), grass_bake.h:1174 (uSkirt = live blade height / cos(pitch))
grass_bake.h.why: A vertical blade of height h covers ground up to h*cot(theta) BEHIND its root, where theta is the elevation of the view ray, not h/cos(theta). Pitch here is elevation below the horizontal: n64_eye builds forward = (0,-sin p,-cos p) (cnc_eyes.cpp:5947-5960) and the range is 0.78 to 0.92 rad, 44.691 to 52.712 deg (cnc_eyes.cpp:5455-5458). The vertical fov is 50 deg (cnc_eyes.cpp:5461, N64_F = 1/tan(25 deg) at :5463), so the top row of the frame looks along a ray 25 deg shallower than the nominal pitch. I measured the true band numerically through the engine's own projection (n64_eye plus project_point, F = 2.14450692, 720 rows), for h = 0.435 cells (the bake's own height ceiling 0.30 x 1.45): far zoom (p = 52.712 deg) 0.344 cells at the frame centre and 0.860 cells at the top row; near zoom (p = 44.691 deg) 0.471 cells at the centre and 1.301 cells at the top row. grass_sd_range_of bakes 0.30*1.45/cos(0.92) = 0.718 cells and the draw fades over h/cos(p), which is 0.718 cells at far zoom and 0.612 at near zoom.
grass_bake.h.consequence: Two visible failures at once, from the same scalar. TOO NARROW at the top of the frame: at near zoom the blade's ink reaches 1.301 cells while the fade band ends at 0.612 cells and the baked distance cannot even EXPRESS more than 0.718 cells, so blades in the 0.6 to 1.3 cell band draw at full alpha over object silhouettes and over the void. That is exactly the dark halo contract B exists to prevent, restored across the top third of every frame and unfixable in the draw because the vertex sd has already saturated. TOO WIDE in the lower half: at the frame centre and bottom the fade is 2.1x and 7.3x the blade's real reach, so a bald strip of about half a cell (12 art texels) is cut along every shoreline and along the whole inner edge of the play rectangle where no grass needed removing. Under the isometric row (perspective = FX_PERSP_ISO) the narrow case gets far worse: iso_pitch floors at iso_fov/2 + 2, and with iso_fov at its minimum 25 that is 14.5 deg (fx_state.h:622-625, cnc_eyes.cpp:5528-5533), where cot at the top row exceeds 28 and the band is over ten cells.
grass_bake.h.fix: Rename the field pitch_min and fill it from the SHALLOWEST reachable pitch, then bake r = height_ceiling * (1 + vary_ceiling) * cot(pitch_min - fovy/2) with the existing GRASS_SD_MAX clamp made loud when it bites, the way the grid and budget refusals already are. In the contract, uSkirt must be live_h * cot(elevation) rather than live_h / cos(pitch); since the elevation varies with the screen row, the honest form is per fragment from the view ray, and a single uniform must use the top-of-frame elevation so it is never short.

grass_bake.h.what: The CM tint is dropped from the interface the draw path is handed, although the file's own colour_build comment says it belongs there.
grass_bake.h.why: grass_colour_build's comment states correctly that the console's combiner is out = (texel - tint) * lit and that BOTH terms belong in the live per-corner texture. But the enumerated handoff at :1163 names only "the per corner light term (oneSun ? 160/255 : terrain_shade) times shroud_corner_vis, and the crush field", the uniform list at :1170-1175 exports no tint, and the list is prefaced "which the draw must not invent for itself". The tint is not hypothetical: it is on by default (g_cmTint, cnc_eyes.cpp:1262), draw_terrain applies it whenever terrain_tint_live() is true (cnc_eyes.cpp:6707, :6821-6824) via a GL_SUBTRACT stage, and I parsed the shipped packs' PKC block directly. SCB01EA carries 898 of 4225 non-black corners with 5-bit maxima (26,19,16), which through terrain_tint_calc's lit*c5*200/32768 at lit = 160 gives a per-channel tint up to 25 of 255 with a mean of 3.8. SCG01EA carries 248 non-black corners, up to 14.
grass_bake.h.consequence: On every pack with a live CM layer the blade root keeps a colour the ground beside it had subtracted, so the root sits up to 25 levels of 255 brighter than the ground and, because the tint is per channel and redder than it is blue on these packs, hue-shifted warm against it. That is the "sticker" the file's own comment names, at about a fifth of the 59% magnitude it warns about, concentrated exactly where the artist placed a colour change.
grass_bake.h.fix: Add the tint to the live half at :1163 and to the uniform list at :1170-1175: the per-corner texture must carry terrain_tint_shrouded(cx, cz, shroud_corner_vis) as well as the light, and the draw's root colour must be (stored atlas RGB minus tint) * light, matching cnc_eyes.cpp:6498-6501.

grass_bake.h.what: The draw-order slot given for grass_draw permits it to be placed after the shroud blanket, which is the one placement that produces the exact failure contract G is written to prevent.
grass_bake.h.where: grass_bake.h:1153-1156 ("after the opaque and cutout passes ... and before fx_world_end")
grass_bake.h.why: The stated hazard at grass_bake.h:940-947, that a tall blade "depth rejects" the blanket, cannot occur: grass is specified with glDepthMask(GL_FALSE) at :1155-1156, so it writes no depth and can reject nothing. The real dependency is ordering. shroud_dispatch_draw runs at cnc_eyes.cpp:20980, before the seam at :21053, and the blanket paints black over the ground at per-vertex alpha a = shroud_corner_a (shroud_mod.h:731-745). The terrain has ALREADY been multiplied by 1 - a in its vertex alpha, so a ground pixel under the feather band ends at albedo*(1-a)^2, while a blade drawn after the blanket with only the vertex shroud term ends at albedo*(1-a). The named window at :1153-1156 contains both sides of :20980 and does not say which.
grass_bake.h.consequence: If grass_draw is placed anywhere between cnc_eyes.cpp:20980 and :21053, grass over mapped-but-unseen ground is 1.8x brighter than the ground it stands on at a = 0.45, and 4.6x brighter in the feather band where a is capped at SHROUD_SOFT_MAXA 0.784 (shroud_mod.h:486). That is lit grass on unexplored map, drawn in a bright ring along the whole reveal perimeter.
grass_bake.h.fix: Pin the slot: grass_draw must be called before shroud_dispatch_draw (cnc_eyes.cpp:20980), and say so at :1153-1156. Replace the depth-rejection sentence at :940-947 with the ordering requirement, which is the thing that is actually load bearing.

grass_bake.h.what: The shoreline is listed as one of the silhouette edges the skirt protects, but water pixels are not silhouettes in this engine: they carry gn.a = 1.0 and are lit as ground.
grass_bake.h.where: grass_bake.h:1177-1180 ("a dark halo one blade tall around the base of every structure, every unit, every shoreline and the whole map rim"), driving the water veto at grass_bake.h:610-613 and the skirt it feeds
grass_bake.h.why: fx_draw_terrain_normals iterates every cell_shown cell and does NOT skip c.holes, and it runs with glDisable(GL_ALPHA_TEST) (cnc_eyes.cpp:19856-19882), so the full terrain quad rasterises over a water cell. fx_world_end binds it against the scene depth with GL_LEQUAL and glPolygonOffset(-1,-2) pulling it toward the viewer (fx_post.h:911-921), and the seabed under it is drawn from the same corner vertices (cnc_eyes.cpp:6984-6994), so the quad passes and writes gn.a = 1.0. In the light pass that gives ground = 1 (fx_post.h:233) and the AO weight stays at ssao_ground, not 1.0. The map rim past rect + margin is a genuine silhouette, but g_terrainMargin is 4 (cnc_eyes.cpp:6411), so the four cells just outside the play rectangle are drawn, are in the normal pass, and are lit like ground too.
grass_bake.h.consequence: The file spends a 0.718-cell skirt around every lake, river and coast, and around the inner edge of the play rectangle, to prevent a halo that cannot occur at either place. Combined with defect 1's over-wide fade in the lower half of the frame, the visible result is a bald verge of roughly half a cell of bare sand between the grass and the water on every temperate map, where the blade's real reach is 0.1 to 0.35 cells there.
grass_bake.h.fix: Keep the water veto if grass floating over the sea is unwanted on its own merits, but size its skirt from the blade's measured reach (defect 1's cot form) rather than from the halo argument, and correct the sentence at :1177-1180 so the next reader does not size a different mechanism from a false premise. The halo list should name objects only.

grass_bake.h.what: The vertex table's stated saturation for the sd field is wrong by a factor of 2.8 against what the code writes.
grass_bake.h.where: grass_bake.h:30-33 ("in 1/256 cell, saturating at 512 = 2.000 cells") against grass_bake.h:777 and grass_bake.h:1093
grass_bake.h.why: grass_emit_tile writes grass_short(b.sd * GRASS_SD_STEP), and b.sd is capped by grass_skirt_dist at g_grassSdRange, which grass_bake sets from grass_sd_range_of. At the defaults that is 0.718 cells, so the largest sd ever written is 184, not 512. No constant in the file equals 512: GRASS_SD_MAX is 8.0 cells, which would be 2048.
grass_bake.h.consequence: The vertex table is the contract the draw's shader is written from. Anyone sizing the fade or a debug visualisation from "2.000 cells" is wrong by 2.8x in the direction that makes grass vanish over more than two cells of ground around every blocked cell, and the error is silent because uSdRange carries the real number in a different place.
grass_bake.h.fix: State the saturation as g_grassSdRange, computed by grass_sd_range_of and exported as uSdRange, and give the default figure beside it rather than a literal that matches nothing.

grass_bake.h.what: The tile's world-y bracket covers only the roots, so it under-reports the tile's real vertical extent by a full blade height.
grass_bake.h.where: grass_bake.h:272 ("world y bracket of its roots, for the cull"), grass_bake.h:803-811
grass_bake.h.why: ylo and yhi are taken from b.y, the root height from terrain_y, and nothing adds height_ceiling * (1 + vary_ceiling). A blade's tip stands 0.435 cells above y1 at the bake ceiling. Under a pitched camera a higher point projects higher on screen (the same fact shroud_draw_soft states for its own lid at shroud_mod.h:642-647), so a tile whose roots are just below the bottom edge of the frustum has tips inside it.
grass_bake.h.consequence: A frustum cull built from the tile box drops tiles whose blades are visible, so grass pops in and out along the bottom edge of the screen as the camera scrolls. Because the cull is per tile, the pop is 4 cells wide at a time.
grass_bake.h.fix: Set t.y1 = yhi + cfg.height_ceiling * (1.0f + cfg.vary_ceiling) so the bracket describes the geometry the tile actually draws, and say in the comment that it is the blade extent and not the root extent.

grass_bake.h.what: The sampling convention for the LIVE per-corner texture is not stated, and it cannot be the one the bake exports.
grass_bake.h.where: grass_bake.h:1172 (uFieldScale = (1/g_gridW, 1/g_gridH), annotated to g_grassGroundTex) with grass_bake.h:1163, under the preface at grass_bake.h:1166 ("which the draw must not invent for itself")
grass_bake.h.why: The static field is per CELL, gridW x gridH, and wx/gridW lands on the cell centre, which I verified is right. The live half the file requires is per CORNER: draw_terrain reads shroud_corner_vis and terrain_shade at (cx,cy) through (cx+1,cy+1) (cnc_eyes.cpp:6795-6814), a (gridW+1) x (gridH+1) lattice whose sample i sits at world x = i, so its correct texcoord is (wx + 0.5)/(gridW + 1), not wx/gridW. The file exports only the cell scale and names no second one, in a list it says the draw must not invent for itself.
grass_bake.h.consequence: A draw that follows the preface and reuses uFieldScale for the corner field misregisters the light and shroud lattice by a linear drift reaching half a cell at the map edges, so the shroud reveal edge on the grass sits half a cell away from the same edge on the terrain, which reads as a bright or dark grass fringe that walks along the reveal boundary as it moves.
grass_bake.h.fix: Export a second scale beside uFieldScale, for example uCornerScale = (1/(g_gridW+1), 1/(g_gridH+1)) with a +0.5 texel offset, and say in the same list that the two fields have different registrations. One line, and it removes the trap the preface was written to close.

grass_bake.h.what: grass_bake_sync has no failure latch, so on every map where grass refuses itself the entire bake re-runs from scratch every single frame. The file explicitly directs the draw path to call this on its first line every frame (line 1110), and the expensive work is paid BEFORE any of the three refusals can fire: grass_mask_build runs at line 1097, and grass_geometry_build at 1098 only reaches its VBO budget test at 844 after the full count pass, while grass_buf_load sits at 819 INSIDE that second call, so a driver with no vertex buffer objects pays the whole mask build first and throws it away. The author already knows the idiom: grass_buf_load latches itself with g_grassBufTried at lines 216-217. The bake does not.
grass_bake.h.where: grass_bake.h:1126 (`if (!g_grassHave) return grass_bake(cfg);`), with the three refusals at 580-584, 844-857 and 1084-1090, and the ordering at 1097-1099 and 819
grass_bake.h.why: Measured with a probe replicating grass_mask_build, grass_blade_at, grass_skirt_dist, terrain_y and grass_emit_tile verbatim in shape (a scratch probe). Case a, no VBO entry points: grass_bake.h:1097 runs the full mask build and grass_bake.h:819 then refuses, so the cost is 16.25 ms per frame on a 64x64 grid, thrown away. Case b, USER91.pack, which I confirmed is 128x128 TEMPERAT by reading its PKF dims at byte offset 12 of playable/USER91.pack: mask 66.91 ms plus count pass 40.89 ms = 107.80 ms per frame before the budget refusal at 844 fires. Case c, the theater gate at 580: I parsed every pack in playable/ and 46 of the 94 are DESERT (43), SAND (1), SNOW (1) or WINTER (1), none of which clears the +0.08 gate, and each costs a measured 0.0388 ms plus one unbuffered stderr line of 77 bytes, every frame.
grass_bake.h.consequence: Against the stated 1.6 ms frame budget: 16.25 ms is 10x over, on ANY driver without VBOs and on all 48 temperate packs, which defeats the exact promise the file makes for itself at lines 96-101 (a driver without vertex buffer objects was supposed to lose grass and keep everything else, and instead it loses ten frame budgets a frame for ever). 107.80 ms is 67x over, roughly 9 fps, on a real shipped file. The theater gate case is only 2.3 percent of CPU but writes about 4.6 KB a second of duplicate stderr, which the gate scripts capture, so a one minute gate run grows 277 KB of one repeated line. Today the storm is latent because grass_draw.h never calls grass_bake_sync at all; it lands the moment the call site is written the way line 1110 directs.
grass_bake.h.fix: Add a g_grassBakeTried latch beside g_grassBufTried (grass_bake.h:198), set on every exit from grass_bake and cleared in exactly one place, where the sync guard's other keys change (scen, grid, rect, cfg at 1127-1137), so a refusal is announced once and costs one branch thereafter. Separately, move the grass_buf_load() call from grass_geometry_build:819 to the top of grass_bake, before grass_mask_build:1097, so a driver with no buffer objects never pays for a mask it cannot use.

grass_bake.h.what: The 64x64 CPU memory figures in the header table are sized by the PLAY RECTANGLE while the code sizes both arrays by the GRID, and the file contradicts itself about the same number 1134 lines later. Line 65 states 276,768 B of CPU mask and 15,376 B of per cell colour; both are 62 based (62*24 = 1488, 1488 squared over 8 = 276,768; 62*62*4 = 15,376). The code at line 596 sizes the mask as g_gridW * GRASS_MASK_RES and at line 959 sizes the colour as g_gridW * g_gridH * 4, both from the grid.
grass_bake.h.where: grass_bake.h:65, against the code at 596 and 959, and against the file's own line 1199
grass_bake.h.why: The probe on a 64 wide grid produces 294,912 B of mask and 16,384 B of colour texture, not 276,768 and 15,376. The file's own line 1199 says the kept arrays cost 295 KB, which agrees with the code and disagrees with line 65. In the SAME paragraph the arithmetic ceiling row (524,288 blades = 64*64*128) and the whole 256x256 row are grid based, and the probe reproduces the 256 row's 4,718,592 B of mask exactly, so the two rows in that paragraph were not produced by the same code path.
grass_bake.h.consequence: The paragraph is offered as figures that are RUN and not derived, so a reader sizing the residency ring the file recommends at limitation 4 gets a rectangle shaped answer for a grid shaped allocation. The absolute error is only 19,152 B, but it is the one paragraph anyone will quote when deciding whether the whole map buffer fits, and half of it did not come out of this code.
grass_bake.h.fix: Correct line 65 to 294,912 B of CPU mask and 16,384 B of per cell colour, and make line 1199 read 369 KB rather than 295 KB, since the kept arrays are 294,912 plus 4,096 x3 plus 70,656 of tile records = 377,856 B.

grass_bake.h.what: height_ceiling is documented as the top of the height dial's RANGE and set to 0.30, but the dial's range top is 0.35. vary_ceiling is 0.45 against a variation dial that runs to 0.80. The comment block at 302-306 and the struct comment at 296 both assert these are the range tops, and the sync guard at 1134-1135 compares them, so a stale value is invisible rather than caught.
grass_bake.h.where: grass_bake.h:307-308, against a scratch probe:61 (0.03f, 0.35f) and :67 (0.0f, 0.80f)
grass_bake.h.why: I checked whether this can actually starve the skirt and it cannot, at any point in the shipped ranges. The draw's uSkirt is g_fx.grass_height / cos(pitch) (grass_draw.h:696-699) and does not use vary at all, so its maximum is 0.35 / cos(0.92) = 0.578 cells against a baked saturation g_grassSdRange = 0.30 * 1.45 / cos(0.92) = 0.7188 cells. The baked band is 24 percent wider than the widest the draw can ask for, so it is conservative, never short. The cost of correcting it is measured: setting the ceilings to the true 0.35 and 0.80 raises g_grassSdRange to 1.041, which raises g_grassSdCells from 1 to 2 and the skirt search from 9 to 25 rectangle tests a blade, taking the 64x64 bake from 41.0 ms to 49.5 ms (mask 18.3, count 12.9, write 18.2).
grass_bake.h.consequence: Nothing goes wrong today, and I want to be plain about that rather than inflate it. What it costs is that the file's stated rule and its constant disagree, in the one place the sync guard cannot catch, so the first person who widens the height dial gets a skirt baked from a ceiling that is no longer the ceiling and a band that silently under-covers, with no assert and no log line naming it.
grass_bake.h.fix: Either set height_ceiling to 0.35f and vary_ceiling to 0.80f and accept the measured 8.5 ms of extra load time, or change the comments at 296 and 302-306 to say these are a chosen conservative bound rather than the dial's range, and add a one line stderr note when grass_sd_range_of clamps or when the live uSkirt would exceed g_grassSdRange.

grass_bake.h.what: GRASS_SD_MAX is 8.0 cells and nothing between the height dial and the bake warns that the skirt search is quadratic in it. g_grassSdCells is ceil(g_grassSdRange) at line 1093, and both grass_mask_build's near-block pass (664-678) and grass_skirt_dist (686-708) are O((2R+1) squared) with a sqrtf inside, the latter per blade and paid twice because the count pass runs it too.
grass_bake.h.why: Measured on the 64x64 case: at the default R=1 the count pass is 12.0 ms; at R=2 it is 13.0 ms; at R=4 it is 28.4 ms; at the clamp's own ceiling R=8 it is 122.6 ms, so the total bake goes from 41 ms to roughly 270 ms. That is a lower bound, because my synthetic map only has blocked cells at the border, so far fewer cells are flagged near-block than on a real map with scattered water and cliffs.
grass_bake.h.consequence: A designer who raises height_ceiling toward 1.2 cells to try a taller blade gets a six times slower load with nothing in the log saying why, since the mask line at 649-654 prints g_grassSdRange but never g_grassSdCells, which is the number that actually drives the cost. Combined with the missing latch above, on a refused map that becomes a 270 ms per frame loop instead of a 108 ms one.
grass_bake.h.fix: Print g_grassSdCells alongside skirt=%.3f in the mask line at 649-654, and refuse or warn loudly above about R=3 the same way the grid and budget gates already do, rather than silently clamping at 8.

grass_bake.h.what: The two client-array timings quoted in the opening argument do not follow from the transfer rate quoted beside them, for this file's own 16 byte vertex.
grass_bake.h.why: 268k vertices at 16 bytes is 4.29 MB; the quoted 5 ms is 0.86 GB/s. 1.34M vertices is 21.44 MB; the quoted 39 ms is 0.55 GB/s. Neither is inside the quoted 1.1 to 1.4 GB/s. Adding the client index array (134k and 1072k triangles at 6 bytes) only moves them to 0.96 and 0.72 GB/s. The batching design's own table carries the same 5.31 and 38.62 ms against a vertex that is also 16 bytes (a scratch probe:61-70), so the inconsistency is inherited faithfully rather than introduced here.
grass_bake.h.consequence: Nothing at runtime, and the conclusion the paragraph draws is right by 50x either way. But at the rate the file states, a per frame client array rebuild of the same geometry would cost 3.1 and 15.3 ms, not 5 and 39, so anyone re-deriving a budget from the rate gets a different answer from the one the file hands them two lines later.
grass_bake.h.fix: Quote either the measured times or the measured rate, not both, and say which vertex size the times were taken at. If the rate is kept, state it as 0.55 to 0.96 GB/s for this vertex, which is what the times imply.

grass_bake.h.what: gr_glBufferData's result is never checked, and on this driver a failed store is completely silent
grass_bake.h.why: Measured on the real context (AMD Radeon PRO W6800X, GL 2.1 ATI-7.1.6): glBufferData at 48 MiB and 512 MiB succeeds and GL_BUFFER_SIZE reads back the full size; at 4 GiB and 32 GiB it returns GL_NO_ERROR, GL_BUFFER_SIZE reads 0, and a glDrawArrays from that buffer also returns GL_NO_ERROR and draws nothing. There is no glGetError check and no glGetBufferParameteriv anywhere in the file, and glGetBufferParameteriv is not in the five-pointer group at :191-195. The engine's own precedent is the opposite: fx_gl.h:400-406 checks glCheckFramebufferStatus and prints FX|rt|... incomplete before freeing.
grass_bake.h.consequence: This is the only GL call in the file that can fail at runtime, and it is the one carrying the largest allocation the program makes (up to GRASS_VBO_BUDGET, 48 MiB, measured 19.71 MiB on SCB31EA). On a VRAM-constrained machine the store is not created, grass_bake still runs to :1106 and sets g_grassHave = 1, and grass_draw then draws from a zero-sized buffer: no grass, no GL error, no message, and a GRASS|vbo line in the log claiming the bytes were uploaded. That is exactly the silent half-load the file's own preamble (:96-101) and fx_gl.h:27-29 say the design exists to prevent, and it is indistinguishable from a shader or draw-order bug.
grass_bake.h.fix: Add glGetBufferParameteriv to the optional buffer group (a sixth pointer, resolved the same way, folded into g_grassBufReady). After each gr_glBufferData: drain glGetError, then read GL_BUFFER_SIZE back and compare against the size just requested. On a short or zero store, print a GRASS|refused line naming the requested bytes and the size the driver actually made, delete both buffers and return false, so grass_bake falls through its existing failure path instead of reporting success.

grass_bake.h.what: A refused bake is never memoised, so grass_bake_sync re-runs the entire failed bake on every single frame
grass_bake.h.where: grass_bake.h:1126 (`if (!g_grassHave) return grass_bake(cfg);`), with the failure exits at :1085-1092, :1097, :1098 and :1099 all leaving g_grassHave at 0
grass_bake.h.consequence: Measured with the real header on real shipped packs. USER91.pack (128x128, temperate) is refused by GRASS_VBO_BUDGET after the mask pass, and every further grass_bake_sync call costs 133.64 ms (30 calls, 4009.3 ms total): the full 3072x3072 mask over 8,484,147 texels plus the whole count pass, rebuilt every frame, forever, on a map where grass draws nothing. That is roughly 7 fps for the rest of the mission, plus two lines to stderr per frame. On the four theatre banks that fail the gate at :568-573 it is cheaper but permanent: SCB01EA and USER01 (DESERT) cost 0.0204 ms and one `GRASS|off|theater DESERT ...` line per frame for ever, which buries the gate logs the project reads. The 256-cell refusal at :1085 is one fprintf per frame. water_field_sync has the same shape, but its failure path is a fraction of the cost and does not print.
grass_bake.h.fix: Give the refusal a memory. grass_bake.h.what: The bake does not leave GL exactly as it found it: it sets GL_TEXTURE_BINDING_2D to 0 on whichever texture unit is active, instead of restoring what was there
grass_bake.h.where: grass_bake.h:457 (`glBindTexture(GL_TEXTURE_2D, 0)` at the end of grass_atlas_readback) and :1033 (the same at the end of grass_colour_build)
grass_bake.h.why: State audit over 21 GL items around a real grass_bake_sync call in the world pass: exactly one changes, GL_TEXTURE_BINDING_2D. Under --enhanced it goes 965 -> 0 (the terrain atlas the frame had bound), in the default tier 1 -> 0. A second probe with glActiveTexture on GL_TEXTURE1 confirmed the clobber follows the active unit, not unit 0. The file's own preamble makes no note of it, and its declaration comment at :1146-1148 tells the draw path to call grass_bake_sync on its first line without saying what that call consumes.
grass_bake.h.consequence: Benign only while every consumer rebinds. It is a live trap for the caller: the texset-flip branch at :1152-1153 runs grass_colour_build in the middle of a frame, so if grass_bake_sync is ever placed anywhere but immediately before grass's own glBindTexture calls, the next draw samples texture object 0 (white, or the last thing left in the default object) with no GL error at all. The rest of the file is measurably clean on this point, so the one exception is worth closing rather than leaving to be rediscovered.
grass_bake.h.fix: Three lines in each of the two functions: `GLint prev = 0; glGetIntegerv(GL_TEXTURE_BINDING_2D, &prev);` before the first bind, and `glBindTexture(GL_TEXTURE_2D, (GLuint)prev);` in place of the `0` at :457 and :1033. Then the audit reports zero changed state and the call site stops mattering.
